newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Codelco reports no snags due to storms.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Codelco reports no snags due to storms.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco said on Monday it had not suffered any major problems due to a storm that hit Chile's central region.
Codelco communications manager Christian Calderon said that unlike June's downpours, which crippled El Teniente division, these recent rains had not disrupted operations.
"We've had no reports from the division regarding any specific problems," he said in a telephone interview.
The tempest forced Chilean authorities to close six ports over the weekend: Valaparaiso, San Antonio, Quinteros, Talcahuano, Lirquen and Coquimbo.
El Teniente uses San Antonio to ship copper but Calderon played down its closing, pointing out that a brief shutdown would not seriously upset deliveries.
"Storms usually don't last over 48 hours in Chile," he said.

The Interior Ministry's National Office of Emergencies said Talcahuano and Lirquen, the two more southern ports, had reopened on Monday. The others may resume operations Tuesday or Wednesday once weather conditions improve.
The storms also cut off Chile's main highway, the PanAmerican Route, at several points between Santiago and La Serena, 800 km (500 miles) north of the capital.
Thousands of inhabitants of smaller towns were isolated as mudslides blocked minor roads and over 1,000 people were put up in shelters after their homes were flooded.
